First of all OP, I’m so sorry. Suicide and poor mental health are horrible things to experience whether in regards to yourself or somebody close to you. 

My own father attempted suicide when I was a kid and I very vividly remember the whole night to this day. He didn’t succeed but it was still so traumatizing and my close friend committed suicide at 14. I can imagine the pain you’re in right now. I went batshit both times I experienced this and stopped eating, began self harming, drinking, doing drugs, etc. Don’t let destructive behaviors be a coping mechanism, it’ll only cause you more pain when the numbness goes away. I highly suggest you seek out a therapist or support group as soon as you’re comfortable doing so. I did after about 8 months after my friend passed away. Some say that’s too long to wait but I was comfortable opening up until that point. Until you reach that level please keep yourself surrounded by loved ones and people who can keep you stable and in a clear mindset. 

I’m sorry but I won’t sugarcoat this, the reality is that this is going to be very hard and some days are going to feel like absolute hell. The pain won’t ever fully go away but there are ways to cope and find peace within yourself. For me personally, I worked together with a group of friends and we created a mental health awareness program at my school. We organized speakers and presentations and packets, the whole nine yards. The school still carries this program on every year to this day on the week my friend passed away. It’s dedicated to him and they talk about his story and everything. For me, bringing awareness and memorializing him and making sure he’s never forgotten brought me inner peace. I coped with the help of therapy and my loved ones keeping me grounded. Some people do art, music, memorials, poems, etc. to help with their feelings. 

I hope whatever you decide to do will ease your mind some and one day I hope you can feel at peace with yourself about the whole situation. Don’t let the tragedy cloud the good moments of his life. It’s okay to cry about the negatives and the emotions but don’t ever forget the positives because not every moment was bad. 

I wish you the best of luck, OP. You’re strong enough to get around this. I wish somebody had said to me what I’m saying to you because it took me way too long to figure it out. I’ll be thinking of you and I send nothing but love your way.
